# Layout

Each line: `ID — rule — what to do on the web`. Details and sources: docs/rules/layout.md.

## Must

LAY-01 — Keep content and controls inside the safe area, clear of notches, the home indicator, rounded corners and browser bars. — Set viewport-fit=cover in the viewport meta and pad fixed headers, tab bars, bottom sheets and map controls with env(safe-area-inset-top|right|bottom|left, 0px); full-bleed maps and imagery may extend underneath. The safe-area check flags viewport-fit=cover when a side's inset is never used.
LAY-04 — Base layout decisions on the space actually available, never on the device type or its orientation. — Switch layouts with width media or container queries at the regular breakpoint token (700px by default, overridable per project, for example 761px); no user-agent sniffing and no orientation queries for layout.
LAY-05 — Offer the same functions at every size, changing only how much of it is visible at once. — A wide screen may show a side panel next to the map where a phone uses a sheet or a More menu, but both reach every action.
LAY-12 — Size full-height panes and sheets by the visible viewport so browser toolbars and the on-screen keyboard never cover their controls. — Use 100dvh (with a 100vh fallback first) for full-height layouts and cap sheets with max-height in dvh; dvh ignores the iOS keyboard, so keep controls above it with window.visualViewport resize and scroll events, and add interactive-widget=resizes-content to the viewport meta for Chromium.
LAY-19 — Let content reflow at 320 CSS pixels wide so nothing needs scrolling in two directions, except content such as maps, data tables and diagrams that needs both. — At 320px every span fits the compact grid's 4 columns and side-by-side items stack; no page container, grid track or min-width is wider than the viewport; give text overflow-wrap break-word so long words, URLs and IDs wrap instead of spilling out of their column; wide tables and code blocks scroll inside their own container with overflow-x auto, never the whole page. Test at 320px wide, or at 1280px wide zoomed to 400%.

## Should

LAY-02 — Arrange each screen by importance, placing what matters most at the top and on the leading side. — On a detail page the name, grade and key action come first; secondary details such as history and sources follow; use logical properties (inline-start) so the leading side flips in right-to-left text.
LAY-03 — Leave about 12 points around controls with a visible bezel and about 24 points around bare icons or text controls. — Separate adjacent bordered buttons and chips by the bezel spacing token and bare icon buttons by the bare spacing token, measured from their visible edges (gap or margin).
LAY-06 — Use the standard side margins, 16 points in compact widths and 20 points in regular widths. — Pad page content inline by the compact margin token below the regular breakpoint and by the regular margin token above it, added to the safe-area inset rather than replacing it.
LAY-07 — Keep spacing on the 4-point grid by taking every gap, padding and margin from the space scale. — Write var(--df-space-*) or the Tailwind spacing keys from the preset instead of arbitrary pixel values; the grid check flags padding, margin, gap, inset, size and radius px values that are not a multiple of 4 (2px allowed).
LAY-08 — Align items to shared edges for easy scanning, and indent only to show that an item belongs beneath the one above. — List rows share one leading text edge; problem variations indent under their parent problem by one step of the space scale.
LAY-09 — Group related items and set unrelated ones apart using whitespace, a shared container or a separator. — Put each wall's problems in one card on bg.secondary, divide rows with the separator role, and leave a larger space step between groups than within them.
LAY-10 — Show the essentials first and reveal detail on request. — Use details and summary, expandable sections or a sheet for long approach notes, full FA history and per-problem variations; the collapsed state still names what is inside.
LAY-11 — Make controls look distinct from content, and let full-screen content run underneath bars and floating controls. — The map fills the viewport under the header and tab bar; buttons over it sit on a material or solid fill with a separator edge (see MAT-02).
LAY-13 — Make the layout work in every orientation and window size, even if one orientation is the main use. — Do not set orientation in the web manifest unless the app truly cannot work otherwise; test a short landscape phone height, where sheets must scroll.
LAY-14 — Test the smallest and largest layouts first, then the sizes, languages and text settings in between. — Check 320 CSS px wide (small iPhone with Display Zoom), a landscape phone, a wide desktop window, 200% text and long translated strings in responsive devtools and on a real phone.
LAY-16 — On wide screens, limit how long a line of running text can get instead of letting it span the whole window. — Give paragraphs and description blocks max-inline-size around 70ch (centred or leading-aligned in the column), while maps, tables and images may still use the full width.
LAY-17 — On content pages, lay content out on a fluid column grid of 4 columns in compact widths, 8 in regular widths and 12 in expanded widths. — Use display grid with grid-template-columns repeat(var(--df-layout-columns-compact), minmax(0, 1fr)) and column-gap var(--df-layout-gutter-compact), then switch to the regular and expanded column and gutter tokens at the regular (700px) and expanded (1024px) breakpoints, written as 43.75em and 64em so they follow text size (TYP-09); side margins stay those of LAY-06. Write minmax(0, 1fr), not 1fr, so a long word or wide image cannot push a column wider than its share. In Figma, give each frame size a Stretch column layout guide with the same count, gutter and margin. Full-screen maps and tools do not need a column grid.
LAY-18 — Size and place content by spanning whole columns, so its edges fall on column edges and the gutters stay clear, and let only full-bleed media break out of the grid. — Use grid-column span N or line numbers instead of fixed widths, and give each width class a span that fits its column count; because 4, 8 and 12 all divide by 4, a span of 4 gives one card per row in compact, two in regular and three in expanded. Let nested components line up with the page columns through grid-template-columns subgrid rather than a grid of their own. Full-bleed images, maps and coloured bands sit outside the margined grid container and run to the window edges.
LAY-20 — On very wide windows, stop the column grid at the layout maximum width and centre it, instead of stretching the columns without limit. — Give the grid container max-inline-size var(--df-layout-max-width) and margin-inline auto inside a wrapper that keeps the LAY-06 margins; page backgrounds, full-bleed media and full-screen maps may still run to the window edges, and running text inside stays capped by LAY-16.

## Consider

LAY-15 — When background art or imagery meets a new aspect ratio, scale it to fill rather than stretching or boxing it. — Give background and hero images object-fit cover (or background-size cover) with a sensible object-position, never a forced width and height alone; images whose edges carry information, such as diagrams with marked lines, use contain.
